candidates.core_provocation: Two colleagues at a magical office recover memories that have escaped from people’s minds. When one colleague is accidentally erased from everyone’s memory, the other has until sunset to restore her—but the only surviving copy of their years together is inside his own mind, and saving her will cost him those memories.
candidates.why_interesting: The rescue has a clear deadline, while the solution turns the most precious part of their relationship into the sacrifice.

candidates.core_provocation: Two colleagues work in a hidden market where people can sell memories to keep ghosts alive. One colleague has already sold every memory except the one of her friendship with the protagonist, and at midnight she plans to sell that final memory too.
candidates.why_interesting: The protagonist must save someone who is deliberately becoming a stranger, creating both supernatural tension and a painful emotional choice.

candidates.core_provocation: In a kingdom where memories appear as birds, two colleagues discover a bird carrying the memory of one colleague’s death tomorrow. To prevent it, they must destroy the only memory that explains why the two of them ever became friends.
candidates.why_interesting: A concrete supernatural warning forces the characters to choose between changing the future and preserving the past.

parsed.reason_for_choice: The memory market gives the story an immediate deadline, a vivid fantasy setting, and a simple but gripping problem: how can someone stop a loved colleague from forgetting them when forgetting is her own choice? Its bittersweet resolution can emerge naturally from the action rather than from abstract reflection.
